title: Interop migration workshop to Redwood API
summary: Introductory migration workshop focused on mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints and features to Redwood API equivalents. Covered streaming, function calling, embeddings parity, rate limits, batching, and security (VPC/KMS/SSO). Agreed next steps: share parity spreadsheet, run a short token-cost benchmark, provide trial keys for Redwood Hosted and Dedicated evals.
topics: Throughput, batching, and KV cache behavior
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24T15:00:00Z
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Lena Kovac (StratusWave Head of ML), Raj Patel (Platform Eng), Tom Nguyen (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary: quick mapping session, some noisy audio at the start, lots of product questions, few follow-ups.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:22] Lena (StratusWave): hi, lena here, i run ML for search and recommendations, we've been using OpenAI GPT and a mix of Anthropic for chat, evaluating Together for price/perf.
[00:35] Tom (CTO): tom, oversight and infra questions, we care about VPC and SSO, also cost.
[00:42] Raj: raj, platform, will be doing the integration and ops.
[00:50] Maya: great, i'll do a short demo mapping common calls then carlos will deep-dive on latency/caching and dedicated options.
[01:05] Carlos (SE): hi all, small note — some of my spelling or names might come out funky in the transcript, excuse that.
[01:20] Maya: first, we map the typical openai chat completions call to our Redwood API /v1/chat/completions equivalent. payload is almost the same but a couple of param names differ — e.g. "max_tokens" still exists, but our streaming uses chunked events with slightly different event envelopes.
[01:48] Lena: does Redwood support the function calling spec? we've built a lot of tooling around openai function calls.
[02:02] Maya: yes, function calling is supported. we mirror the name/arguments pattern; the main differences: our schema enforcement can be toggled per-route and we add a per-token prefix cache hint that helps with repeated system prompts. sometimes docs show "Redwood functions" or "fn-calls" which is auto-gen in our docs, but it's same idea.
[02:25] Raj: how about streaming partials and reconnect semantics? in prod we stream to websockets and fallback to polling.
[02:40] Carlos: streaming semantics: we send delta chunks as they are generated, same as openai, but we include a "chunk_offset" field for resuming. reconnects can replay from the prefix KV cache so you don't re-gen the whole context — small caveat, if you're using our Dedicated with KV-disabled, resume doesn't work the same way.
[03:10] Tom: what about Together models — they have different tokenizers and context lengths. is there any extra work?
[03:26] Maya: model-wise, we onboard model variants and provide a "compat" shim. for a lot of together/openai/anthropic models we expose them as model tags like "together-gt-repl-1" or "openai-gpt4o" but for parity we recommend mapping by behavior not name: temperature, top_p, stop sequences, and function schema. tokenization differences show up mainly in pricing and token counts in reference benchmarks. we'll share a tokenization mapping sheet.
[03:55] Lena: embeddings — currently using OpenAI embeddings (1536 dim). our vector store expects fixed dims; anthro embeddings were 1024, together had 1792. can redwood do on-the-fly dim alignment or do we need reindexing?
[04:18] Carlos: embeddings are model-specific. Redwood exposes multiple embedding model variants; we do not auto-resize vectors. recommended approach: choose a single embedding model for the POC and reindex, or keep original vectors and store model id so you can run internal cross-encoders. Optimize (sorry, "Redwood Optimize" or sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Optima") provides guidance on which embedding to pick based on recall/cost tradeoffs.
[04:45] Raj: any built-in tooling for bulk reindexing? we have a 5M vector store.
[04:53] Maya: we don't reindex for you, but we provide tooling snippets and a documented best-practice pipeline; for Dedicated customers we can provide support hours to help.
[05:10] Carlos: also note we support sharded bulk ingestion to speed reindexing, and a sample kafk... kafka connector we demoed last month.
[05:28] Lena: security — we are regulated, SOC2 is table stakes. SSO, RBAC, KMS required, also audit logs with retention 7 years ideally.
[05:40] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II, we have SSO via SAML and OIDC, full RBAC, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS and customer HSM options). audit log retention is configurable on Dedicated and Private; hosted tenants have 90-day standard but enterprise retention add-on is available. we'll share the security pack.
[06:05] Tom: VPC/private deployment options? can we host the control plane in our VPC?
[06:15] Carlos: Redwood Private offers a customer-managed control plane where core metadata is in your VPC and we can do air-gapped packages for on-prem. Dedicated is for reserved capacity in our cloud with dedicated GPU pools but not full control-plane in your VPC. if you need full residency and airgap, that's the Private option.
[06:42] Raj: what's the expected time to get a POC running end-to-end?
[06:50] Maya: for a simple parity POC (chat + embeddings) we usually see 2-4 weeks: week 1 parity mapping + security review, week 2 bench and initial integration, week 3 tuning and canary to prod. Dedicated/private increases lead times.
[07:08] Lena: about latency — can you explain batching behavior? we've tuned batching in our openai calls to balance latency and cost.
[07:20] Carlos: our runtime has continuous batching and prefix KV cache; we expose batch windows in the route config. you can set target p50 and a cost cap; the runtime then adapts. also quantized model variants reduce memory but change latency. in practice, we've seen 10-20% cost savings with small latency tradeoffs.
[07:48] Raj: how are fallbacks handled if top-tier model is saturated? we need graceful degradation.
[07:56] Maya: smart routing rules: you can configure fallback to cheaper model variants by policy (latency-first vs cost-first) and we record token-level metrics so you can see impact. A/B rollout and automatic rollback exist in the console.
[08:14] Tom: console walkthrough?
[08:20] Maya: sure, quick share. opening the Redwood Console (note: link shared in chat: https://console.redwood-inference.example/stratuswave/initial). the route page shows per-route token cost, latency p50/p95, and tooling to change batching and cache settings.
[08:40] Lena: is the data in the console ever visible to Redwood employees? we're strict about data access.
[08:48] Carlos: by default, hosted logs are encrypted and accessible only to automated systems; for Dedicated/Private you can set policies to restrict access. we have an audit log of human access events and attestations.
[08:59] Raj: what's the fastest way to try this? we want sample curl examples and a test key.
[09:06] Maya: we'll spin up a trial project and provide short-lived API key for hosted and a dedicated eval seat. we'll also include sample curl and SDK snippets for python/node.
[09:20] Lena: can you show an example of mapping an openai function call to redwood?
[09:28] Carlos: sure, quick paste: in openai you do messages + functions + function_call; in Redwood you do messages + functions and set "call_mode": "auto". the response envelope has "called_function" instead of "function_call" in some older docs — ignore older docs, use the current SDK snippet. (note: some transcripts later show "called_function" as "called_fn", small inconsistencies).
[09:58] Maya: some customers reported minor tag differences when porting streaming client logic, like event names and http chunk boundaries, but it's generally 95% code-compatible.
[10:15] Tom: pricing — we pay token-based for hosted; Dedicated is reserved. any examples of cost delta migrating from openai?
[10:26] Maya: depends heavily on prompt length and batching. for chat-heavy low-latency workloads, Dedicated tends to reduce unit cost by 30-50% at scale. hosted per-token pricing is competitive; we'll run a quick cost benchmark on your traffic.
[10:40] Raj: how do we instrument so we can compare token accounting between openai and redwood? their tokenizers differ.
[10:50] Carlos: we capture raw token counts per model; for cross-vendor comparisons we recommend replaying a sample corpus through each tokenizer and recording deltas. we'll provide the script.
[11:10] Lena: any gotchas with stop sequences and streaming? we had issues where streaming didn't respect stop well and clients got stuck.
[11:20] Carlos: streaming respects stop tokens; the main source of errors is client-side buffering or expecting exact event types. we recommend using our SDK which handles most edgecases; we'll share a node/python example.
[11:40] attendee (background noise) -> Speaker 5: (transcription glitch)
[11:55] Maya: switching gears — POC success criteria? let's define measurable goals.
[12:05] Tom: 1) >= 95% parity on generation quality for top-3 prompts, 2) p95 latency < 800ms for interactive routes, 3) <= 20% delta in month-to-month token costs or better.
[12:25] Lena: also security sign-off by our compliance team and SSO integration.
[12:30] Maya: agreed. we'll add those to the POC plan.
[12:40] Carlos: for benchmarking we'll need a 24-hour replay of traffic sample (or a representative corpus). recommend anonymize any PII first.
[12:55] Raj: can Redwood run benchmarks in our VPC for Dedicated?
[13:05] Carlos: yes — Dedicated evals can be run in a controlled environment; Private is needed for air-gapped. we can schedule a benchmark run.
[13:25] Maya: quick note on rate limits — Hosted has tiered rate limits, but we can set soft limits for evals. Dedicated gives you throughput guarantees.
[13:45] Lena: compliance question: do you provide per-request provenance and model id in logs? we need to trace exactly which model and version generated which output.
[13:55] Carlos: yes, we attach model_id, model_version, route_id, and cryptographic request ids to each log line. those are stored with retention controls.
[14:10] Tom: what about model upgrades and rollouts? we can't have surprise regressions.
[14:20] Maya: Console supports canary rollouts and eval gating. Redwood Optimize (sometimes transcribed "Optimize suite") includes regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can block rollouts if quality drops.
[14:42] Lena: ok let's talk timeline again and who will own what on each side.
[14:50] Maya: i'll be AE lead, carlos is SE lead. from StratusWave side who owns infra?
[15:00] Raj: i'll own the infra integration and coordinate compliance. lena owns evaluation criteria. tom signs off.
[15:10] Maya: good. we'll send a POC deck, parity spreadsheet mapping endpoint fields, and a sample replay script.
[15:20] Carlos: quick technical deep dive — live demo of a parity mapping. sharing screen now (note: some audio dropouts).
[15:35] Carlos: here's a sample messages payload from openai, and here's the Redwood equivalent. notice we map openai's "role": "assistant" messages identically, but we add a route config object for batching and caching. also you'll see callouts for KV cache hints in system messages.
[16:05] Lena: are there SDK breaking changes we should know about for our microservices? we use python fastapi wrapping the openai client.
[16:15] Carlos: SDKs are drop-in similar to openai's but we also provide a smaller shim that matches the openai call signature for quick swaps. some customers simply swap their client import and change the base url. edge cases: streaming event handlers and function-call name fields may need small changes.
[16:40] Raj: about telemetry and cost allocation per tenant — we have internal chargeback.
[16:48] Maya: console exports CSVs of per-route/token usage, and we can integrate with your billing system via webhook. Dedicated gets per-customer tagging too.
[17:05] Tom: any limitation on token window / context length?
[17:12] Carlos: model dependent. we have variants up to 128k in hosted for some models; Dedicated can enable higher windows based on GPU and model. watch out for kv cache eviction policies with very long contexts.
[17:30] Lena: question: how do you handle PII in logs?
[17:36] Maya: we redact PII by default in logs for hosted but for enterprise we can turn off retention and provide customer-managed encryption keys. we'll include the exact flow in the security pack.
[17:58] Raj: do you support private endpoints inside our VPC?
[18:05] Carlos: with Redwood Private you can host endpoints in your VPC and manage network ACLs. Dedicated is less about networking control and more about capacity isolation.
[18:28] Maya: brief pause — any other red flags?
[18:34] Lena: only that we need the parity spreadsheet and tokenization script asap.
[18:40] Maya: we'll share by end-of-day tomorrow.
[18:46] Carlos: technical note — when porting together models watch for tokenization mismatch on stop sequences; some stop tokens may be split differently. we'll provide examples.
[19:05] attendee (crosstalk): "yeah" / "mm-hmm"
[19:12] Tom: ok, let's define next steps and owners.
[19:20] Maya: recap: Redwood -> send parity spreadsheet, security pack, trial API keys, sample replay script. StratusWave -> provide 24h anonymized traffic sample and list of top-3 prompts for quality test. We'll schedule a 2-hour bench run next week.
[19:45] Lena: that works.
[19:50] Raj: timeline — bench next wed, security review week after.
[19:56] Maya: noted. any final quick questions?
[20:02] Lena: no, thanks, good session.
[20:07] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links and timing.
